questions.prompt: Let \(U=span\)(\((1,0)\)) and \(W=span\)(\((0,1)\)) in \(\mathbb R^2\). Find U + W.
questions.answer: The sum U + W consists of all vectors u + w with u in U and w in W. A vector in U has form \((a,0)\), and a vector in W has form \((0,b)\). Their sum is \((a,b)\). Since a and b can be any real numbers, U + W = \(\mathbb R^2\).

questions.prompt: Let \(U=span\)(\((1,0)\)) and \(W=span\)(\((0,1)\)) in \(\mathbb R^2\). Find U intersection W.
questions.answer: A vector in U has form \((a,0)\), and a vector in W has form \((0,b)\). If a vector is in both, then \((a,0)\) = \((0,b)\). Comparing components gives \(a=0\) and \(b=0\). Therefore U intersection W = {\((0,0)\)}.

questions.prompt: Let U be the xy-plane in \(\mathbb R^3\) and W be the z-axis. Find U + W.
questions.answer: A vector in U has form \((a,b,0)\), and a vector in W has form \((0,0,c)\). Their sum is \((a,b,c)\). Since a, b, and c are arbitrary real numbers, every vector in \(\mathbb R^3\) can be written this way. Therefore U + W = \(\mathbb R^3\).

questions.prompt: Let U be the xy-plane in \(\mathbb R^3\) and W be the z-axis. Find U intersection W.
questions.answer: Vectors in the xy-plane have form \((a,b,0)\). Vectors on the z-axis have form \((0,0,c)\). A vector in both must satisfy \((a,b,0)\) = \((0,0,c)\), so \(a=0\), \(b=0\), and \(c=0\). Therefore the intersection is {\((0,0,0)\)}.

questions.prompt: Let \(U=span\)(\((1,0,0)\), \((0,1,0)\)) and \(W=span\)(\((0,1,0)\), \((0,0,1)\)). Find a basis for U intersection W.
questions.answer: U is the xy-plane, and W is the yz-plane. A vector in U has form \((a,b,0)\). A vector in W has form \((0,c,d)\). For a vector to be in both, its x-component and z-component must be 0, so it has form \((0,t,0)\). Therefore U intersection W is span(\((0,1,0)\)), and a basis is {\((0,1,0)\)}.

questions.prompt: Use \(\dim(U + W)\) = \(\dim(U)\) + \(\dim(W)\) - \(\dim(U intersection W)\). If \(\dim(U)\)=3, \(\dim(W)\)=2, and \(\dim(U intersection W)\)=1, find \(\dim(U + W)\).
questions.answer: Substitute into the dimension formula: \(\dim(U + W)\) = 3 + 2 - 1 = 4. Therefore \(\dim(U + W)\) = 4.

questions.prompt: Let \(U=span\)(\((1,0)\)) and \(W=span\)(\((1,1)\)) in \(\mathbb R^2\). Find U intersection W.
questions.answer: A vector in U has form \((a,0)\). A vector in W has form b(1,1) = \((b,b)\). If \((a,0)\) = \((b,b)\), then the second component gives 0 = b, so \(b=0\). Then \(a=b\) = 0. Therefore the intersection is {\((0,0)\)}.

questions.prompt: Let U = \(\operatorname{span}(1)\) and W = \(\operatorname{span}(x)\) as subspaces of \(P_1\). Find U + W.
questions.answer: A vector in U has form a, and a vector in W has form bx. Their sum is \(a+bx\). Since every polynomial in \(P_1\) has form \(a+bx\), U + W = \(P_1\).

questions.prompt: Let U = \(\operatorname{span}(1)\) and W = \(\operatorname{span}(1+x)\) as subspaces of \(P_1\). Find U intersection W.
questions.answer: A polynomial in U has form a. A polynomial in W has form b\((1+x)\) = b + bx. If \(a=b\) + bx as polynomials, then the x coefficient on the left is 0 and on the right is b, so \(b=0\). Then \(a=0\). Therefore U intersection W = {0}.

questions.prompt: A learner says U + W means union of U and W. Diagnose the error.
questions.answer: The sum U + W is not the union. It is the set of all sums u + w with u in U and w in W. For example, if U is the x-axis and W is the y-axis in \(\mathbb R^2\), then U union W is just the two axes, but U + W is all of \(\mathbb R^2\). The learner confused set union with subspace sum.
